story.title: The Problem
story.body:
Many families throw away food that they forgot they had. Expiry dates get lost at the back of the fridge, and by the time you notice, it is usually too late.

I wanted to create an app that remembers everything for you: what you bought, when it expires and what you can cook with it before then.

story.title: Where It Started
story.body: I started StillGood on my own in April 2026, and designed and built it alongside my freelance projects.
story.callout: From the first line of code to the Google Play Store in about four months.

story.title: What I Built
story.body:
I designed every screen and developed the whole product myself, including the mobile app, the backend server and the website.

Users snap a photo of their groceries and the app lists the items for them. It sorts everything by expiry date, sends a reminder before something expires and suggests recipes that use up the items that need to be eaten first. Households can also share one pantry together.

image.alt: The scanner adding a banana to the pantry

story.title: How It Works
story.body: The app is built with React Native and Expo, with a Fastify server and a Supabase database behind it. Google's Gemini AI reads the grocery photos and suggests recipes, while PostHog shows me how users actually use the app so I can keep improving it.

image.alt: Recipe suggestions that use expiring items

story.title: The Launch
story.body: StillGood went live on the Google Play Store on 26 August 2026, and anyone with an Android phone can now download it for free!
